trust_decision.summary: Per-query metadata filter values (tag, text and numeric) are treated as inert data and interpolated straight into the RediSearch query string handed to `ft.search`; the trust decision is made in the query-string builders themselves (the filter classes' `toString` in filters.ts and `buildCustomQuery`/`prepareFilter` in vectorstores.ts), with no escaping or type check at the redis client boundary.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names unescaped tag/text values, and filters.ts is the file that holds the TagFilter/TextFilter expression builders: TagFilter.toString at 230-239 joins user values into `@field:{...}` and TextFilter.toString at 414-443 interpolates the query into `@field:(...)`; these classes are re-exported from the package entry point (src/index.ts:5) and are the advertised way to filter (README.md:65).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: RedisVectorStore is explicitly deprecated in favour of FluentRedisVectorStore (vectorstores.ts:77-90, README.md:57), so a solver can argue the advisory is about the filter-expression API and that the legacy builder is being retired anyway.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Wildcard text search must keep `*` and `?` unescaped: `Text("title").wildcard("head*")` is expected to render as `@title:(head*)` (asserted at src/tests/filters.test.ts:131-134), so a blanket escaper breaks a legitimate operator. Likewise tag values may legitimately contain the default ',' tag separator, which is what Redis itself splits on at index time (serializeMetadataField, src/schema.ts:352-355), so escaping ',' makes a single value containing it unmatchable.

O6_input_shapes: TagFilter values: single string, string[], Set<string>, and empty array/Set (wildcard branch) — filters.ts:197 and 218-237
TextFilter operators: exact, match, wildcard, fuzzy — filters.ts:392 and 414-439
buildCustomQuery TAG value: scalar string vs array of strings — vectorstores.ts:706-713
buildCustomQuery NUMERIC value: plain number vs {min,max} / {min} / {max} object — vectorstores.ts:690-705
buildCustomQuery TEXT value: single string — vectorstores.ts:714-717
prepareFilter: string[] vs a raw single string — vectorstores.ts:752-757

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Numeric/Timestamp (and Geo) filter classes interpolate their values into the query with no runtime check at all, while the published fix adds exactly that runtime numeric check in the legacy builder
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The constructor parameters are typed `number | [number, number]` (and Geo's as numbers with a unit union), so a solver can say TypeScript already guarantees the value cannot carry query syntax.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point; the mirror check the fix wrote lives one file away in vectorstores.ts:690-705

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Raw query strings are passed through untouched: prepareFilter returns a string filter unchanged (vectorstores.ts:756) and CustomFilter.toString returns its query as-is (filters.ts:558-560)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is a documented raw-query escape hatch ('String arrays or raw query strings', README.md:65; filters.ts:520-530), so a solver can say the caller opted out of escaping on purpose.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file from the landing point, same package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an escaping wrapper (or an explicit raw-query opt-out flag) on the string branch of prepareFilter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix escaped only the array branch of the same helper; the string branch feeds the same `@metadata:(...)` sink, so a maintainer rounding out the API would plausibly add a typed raw wrapper here next.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a widened escapeSpecialChars used by the write path (vectorstores.ts:279) kept in sync with unEscapeSpecialChars (vectorstores.ts:781-786)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same helper name already does the write-side escaping and its inverse; a maintainer making query-time escaping complete would plausibly extend this one for consistency, which is exactly the trap because the inverse must match.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: runtime numeric type validation inside NumericFilter/TimestampFilter.toString, mirroring the check the fix added in buildCustomQuery
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix added that validation in the legacy builder (fix.diff:359-390) but not in the class, so mirroring it into the class is the obvious follow-up a maintainer would write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: escaping or rejecting the tag separator at serialization time so stored tags and queried tags share one representation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Once the query side escapes the separator, a maintainer would plausibly escape it on the write side too; doing so silently changes stored values and breaks round-trips through deserializeMetadataField (schema.ts:434-441).
